transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lyndi Kenyon.
President Trump is attending his second rally
in the battleground state of Georgia
in eight days this evening.
Raul Bali, with member station WABE,
reports the focus is the state's competitive U.S. Senate race
and the open race for governor.
More than 1.6 million Georgians or more than 20%
of active voters have already cast ballots,
but Republican nominee for governor Rick Jackson
who's running to replace term limited
Governor Brian Kemp race concerns this week
about turnout in Republican-heavy rural Georgia.
The hope is Trump's rallies will help with that.
Jackson is running against Democrat
former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms.
The other major race involves U.S. Senator John Ossoff,
the only Democratic senator up for reelection this year
in a state won by Trump in 2024.
He's running against Republican Congressman Mike Collins.
For NPR News, I'm Raul Bali in Atlanta.
- Israeli troops have been forcibly removing residents
from their homes in the occupied West Bank.
The move follows an attack on a military checkpoint
that killed two soldiers and wounded three others yesterday.
NPR's Ruth Sherlock reports.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
has responded to the checkpoint attack
by vowing a military operation in the West Bank
on a scale not seen since Israel
first occupied the territory almost 60 years ago.
The Israeli army is forcibly evicting families
in the Hebron neighborhood
that the Palestinian gunman came from.
The military has also demolished homes
close to the site of the checkpoint attack.
Human rights groups are labeling this collective punishment
and the Israeli rights group at Selim
is calling on foreign governments to act
to prevent what it calls another wave
of ethnic cleansing and war crimes.
Ruth Sherlock, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
- Thunderstorm watches have been in effect today
for parts of the Southwest.
This comes after severe floods across parts of Colorado,
Arizona, New Mexico, and Utah
displaced hundreds of residents.
NPR's Ava Berger spoke to one of those residents.
- It took only 22 days for Juana Puga's house in Utah
to flood again.
- Seriously, like why, why again?
- Puga, her husband, and five young kids
just moved back to their house in Hurricane Utah
on October 1st after a flood in August.
On Thursday morning, Puga stood
in ankle-deep brownish water again.
She describes it as a nightmare.
Her home is one of more than 100 damaged in the city.
- Today, after cleaning up a little bit,
I mean, we're still very sad about our homes,
but it's just, we just lift each other up
and like, okay, we already did this, we can do it again.
- Ava Berger, NPR News.
- You're listening to NPR.
Six Flags says it will add secondary restraints
on its rides across the chain
that are similar to the roller coaster Goliath
at its Georgia Park.
That's where a man died after he was thrown
from his seat.
Melissa Phato from member station WABE has the story.
The seat belts, similar to those worn
in an airplane or car, will be used in addition
to the coaster's mechanical restraints, the company says.
Some Six Flags rides already use these type of restraints.
CEO John Riley did not specify
which attractions will get seat belts,
but eight other rides of the hyper coaster
and giga coaster models manufactured
by the Swiss firm Bolliger and Mabelard
remain closed across the chain.
Goliath also remains closed, depending, quote,
necessary safety reviews and clearances.
Officials are still investigating
what caused 42-year-old Hassan Karim's death
at Six Flags over Georgia.
This is the first major change the company has announced
since the accident earlier this month.
For NPR News, I'm Melissa Phato in Atlanta.
Candy sales are off to a slow start this holiday season
as U.S. consumers face higher living costs
and higher chocolate prices.
The market research firm, Nielsen IQ,
finds Halloween candy sales fell 6.7%
in the month ending October 17th
compared to the same period of time last year.
The National Confectioners Association,
which represents Mars, is much more optimistic
about this year's holiday sales, saying high consumer demand
will likely propel positive Halloween sales
despite concerns about price.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News.
This message comes from Thumbtack.

You can hire top-rated pros, see price estimates,

topics.text: Trump to hold second Georgia rally in eight days, focusing on Senate and governor races
Israeli troops forcibly evict West Bank residents, including Hebron neighborhood, after checkpoint attack
Flooding in Hurricane, Utah damages more than 100 homes, displacing residents again
Six Flags to add secondary seat belt restraints on rides after Georgia Goliath death
Halloween candy sales fall 6.7% in October as consumers face higher prices
